cut: v1 (owner, 19 Oct: backlog pick 3, the Welcome Home sequel; re-premised on the refreshed research: a face counts only when its own new phone is home)
argument: Pear's home screen recognises a face only when that person's own new phone is home and recently unlocked, so grandma with an older phone stays a guest.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word; in Japanese a space marks a reveal segment and is never drawn

text.en: Pear's home screen greets / the family by face. / Does it [know] them?
text.fi: Pearin kotinäyttö tervehtii / perhettä kasvoista. / [Tunteeko] se heidät?
text.ja: Pearの ホーム画面は / 家族を 顔で 迎える。 / 本当に [わかって] いるのか？

captions.source: Pear is the station's name for the real company; HomeView is the real product (launched 13 Oct 2026; ships 13 Nov). It recognises up to six enrolled household members by face and voice (Apple Newsroom via MacRumors, Mac Observer, 13 Oct).

text.en: Only if their own new phone / is home and unlocked [lately].
text.fi: Vain jos oma uusi puhelin / on kotona ja avattu [hiljattain].
text.ja: 自分の 新しい スマホが 家にあり、 / [最近] ロック解除 されていれば。

captions.source: Recognition needs that person's own registered phone or iPad with the maker's AI, on the home Wi-Fi and recently unlocked; 'recently' is not defined (Daring Fireball and 9to5Mac, 13 Oct; Apple's footnotes via MacRumors, Mac Observer). Shown as Mum unlocking it once and putting it back, never as the screen demanding to see it (research-pear-sequel §8.3).

text.en: Grandma's phone is too old. / She stays a [guest].
text.fi: Mummon puhelin on liian vanha. / Hän jää [vieraaksi].
text.ja: おばあちゃんの スマホは 古すぎる。 / ずっと [ゲスト] のまま。

captions.source: Phones without the maker's AI (older than the iPhone 15 Pro) are not recognised; without recognition a person gets the shared guest layer: timers, weather, music, accessories (iPhone in Canada and SmartWorld, 13 Oct; Daring Fireball; MacRumors 'HomeView tidbits', 14 Oct).

text.en: It sees your face. / It asks your [phone].
text.ja: 顔は 見ている。 / でも 聞くのは [スマホ] に。

captions.source: The station's line: the face is seen by the screen, but the phone has to vouch for it.
